relevance_note: The paper describes a cohort of HA20 patients with individual TNFAIP3 frameshift variants, e.g. 'P1 was a 15-year-old female with p.T604Rfs*93'.
method_note: Read the whole paper (a short letter; prose plus figure legends, no tables) and transcribed values by hand into a Python build script; the script only assembles rows and checks spans. Patients are labeled P1-P8; P1-P5 (active disease) are described in the text, P6-P8 (quiescent disease) appear only in the Fig 1C legend and the ISG comparison, so they have individual rows but no variant rows (no variant is given for them). The remaining patients of the 'cohort of twelve' are not described individually and have no rows; healthy volunteers HC1-HC4 and the primary-interferonopathy comparators are not extracted. n_patients_reported = 12 is the authors' cohort size; only 8 HA20 patients are described (5 + 3); note the Fig 1C legend's 'twelve subjects' is 5 + 3 patients + 4 healthy volunteers, a different twelve. Ages for P2-P4 come from 'aged 28, 32, and 61' assigned in listed order (no 'respectively'; no unit stated; ISO assumes years). Ages of P1 and P5 are recorded as age at report; the paper does not say when they were measured. 'orogenital ulcerations (P1-P4)' was recorded as both oral and genital ulcers for each of P1-P4. Zygosity is 'not reported' for every variant: the paper's general statement that HA20 patients carry heterozygous TNFAIP3 mutations is not stated per person. The gene symbol comes from the introduction ('encoded by TNFAIP3'); variants are printed as protein changes only, without a transcript. The second mention prints 'T604Rfs*93' without 'p.'. P5's variant is called 'unreported' (novel), which is recorded here only, not as a pathogenicity class; T604Rfs*93 and p.L626Vfs*45 are said to lie in ZnF4 (domain location, not a functional assay). The luciferase NF-κB statement applies to 'All patients' and is copied to P1-P5 variants; it is not applied to P6-P8, whose cohort membership is not stated, and their clinical_diagnosis_basis is left 'not reported' for the same reason. Evidence-basis convention: 'stated for this individual' when the quoted span names the patient (including label ranges such as 'P1-P4'); 'inferred from group statement' when the statement refers to an explicitly defined group without labels in the sentence ('all five patients'; 'these subjects' = P6-P8; 'during treatment' = the four tofacitinib-treated patients P1, P3, P4, P5). The infection and cardiovascular exclusions concern the treatment period only and are not carried to the checklist (narrow, time-limited absence). P5 was 'asymptomatic', but that was not used to exclude any checklist item; the sentence 'severe hepatic inflammation in the absence of systemic features' does not name P5 and was not used. P5's liver disease is called 'autoinflammatory', not autoimmune, so 'autoimmune hepatitis' is left 'not reported'. P2's 'retinal vasculopathy' was not mapped to uveitis/ocular inflammation or vasculitis. ESR/CRP and AST/ALT are shown in figures, but the text never says they were elevated, so those items are not reported. CONTRADICTION: the main text says 'P2 declined tofacitinib' and 'Clinical and immunologic responses were seen in all four patients', but the figure legends show after-treatment values for P2 ('AIDAI scores (P1-P3)' before/after treatment initiation; 'HA20 after treatment (P1-P5)'; supplementary safety monitoring '(P1-P5)'). The main-text statement is used for P2's treatment. The supplementary legend also labels panels as both '1C-D' and '(1F)'/'(1G)'.
